title: Cosanima per-frontend CI over the validate oracle
goal: Per-frontend CI in each native toolkit that runs build → golden-fixture scan → `cosanima frontend validate`, catching schema drift in the frontend repo, with a golden-fixture diff mode.

target: per-frontend golden fixture corpus + expected JSONL

title: Per-frontend CI lane over the oracle
body: Each of the six frontend repos runs a native-toolkit CI lane: build → run the frontend on a golden fixture → pipe stdout to `cosanima frontend validate`. Schema drift is caught in the frontend repo at CI time, not at the first real scan. The lane consumes the validate oracle built in cosanima-frontend-interface.

title: Golden fixture + diff mode
body: Each frontend repo keeps a committed golden fixture — a canonical sample project for its language plus the expected JSONL. A diff mode (`--update`) refreshes the golden expectations after an intentional, validated schema revision, so the lane compares deterministically rather than failing on every sanctioned change.

title: Pinned compatible oracle binary
body: Each lane resolves and pins a `cosanima` binary whose schema revision is compatible with the frontend's SUPPORTED_COSANIMA (per the handshake in cosanima-frontend-interface), so validate results are reproducible across runs and upgrades.

title: Lanes independent of the core gate
body: Per-frontend CI lanes are independent of the Rust core test gate (source: 'Per-frontend CI lanes ... independent of the Rust core gate'): a frontend repo can fail fast on its own schema drift without waiting on or running the core's test suite.

summary: Schema drift is caught in the frontend repo at CI time, not at the first real scan (source: 'schema drift caught in the frontend repo, not at first real scan') — the validate oracle is the CI gate.

title: Diff mode + adoption across six repos

body: No cross-repo CI orchestration: each frontend repo's lane is self-contained and independent (no shared CI job across the seven repos).
Frontend CI is not a substitute for, nor gated on, the core Rust test gate (that gate lives in the parent release spec's quality feature).
A schema-breaking change to a frontend's output fails that frontend's own CI lane (validate oracle returns non-zero in CI).
Each of the six frontend repos has a green lane: build → golden-fixture scan → validate, and `--update` regenerates golden JSONL deterministically.
Verification: introduce a deliberate schema violation in a frontend's output and confirm its CI lane fails; restore and confirm green.
Verification: run each lane's `--update` and confirm the golden diff is a no-op on an unchanged fixture (idempotent).

source: SPEC-1.0.0.md describes the CI consuming `carto frontend validate` with a golden-fixture diff mode; materialized as `cosanima frontend validate` and cosanima-frontend-ci per the binding name [with user].
